selection_rationale: ac-2026-003 (public benchmark + machine‑checkable validator) scored highest on novelty, falsifiability, reproducibility, and compute feasibility in the critic reviews (verdict: pass). It directly addresses the surveyed community gap for standardized, machine‑checkable NetOps evaluation artifacts, produces concrete, reusable deliverables required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, and has lower ethical/operational risk than adversarial or human‑subject studies. It therefore offers the strongest defensible, reproducible contribution within the venue constraints.
unresolved_uncertainties: Synthetic topologies may fail to capture critical production artifacts and edge cases (external validity).
Deterministic validators may incompletely model stateful or temporal behaviors (validator coverage gap).
Benchmark design choices could bias evaluation toward certain methods (benchmark overfitting).
Community adoption, maintenance, and governance of the released benchmark are uncertain.
Scope/limits of discriminatory power vs. real operational complexity (how well benchmark findings generalize).
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Provide a clear, reproducible topology and intent generation protocol and report coverage/diversity metrics comparing synthetic topologies to public/real traces.
Include a validator test suite with coverage reports, known‑case detection rates, and explicit documentation of limitations (stateless vs stateful behaviors).
Specify licensing, redaction, and responsible‑release policy to avoid exposing sensitive operational data; include artifact hashes and redaction procedures.
Provide containerized baseline runbooks (exact environment, seeds, host‑API versions), baseline results, and exact commands to reproduce published baselines.
Add governance and maintenance plan (versioning, issue tracker, contact, update policy) and guidance to reduce benchmark overfitting by future contributors.
